html:
Performers
Louis Krasner (violin), The Cleveland Orchestra (orchestra), Artur Rodzinski (conductor) Documented

Named in the item description and in the 1941 review, which also states that Krasner suggested the concerto to Berg.

[1] [2]
Work version
Berg’s score for solo violin and orchestra; the edition the performers used is not stated. Unknown

The item description and the 1941 review name the work and the performers but not the printed or manuscript material.

[1]
Recorded
15 December 1940 Documented

Stated in the description written by the transferring collector, in the Sony Classical box-set listing (Discogs, “Cleveland, Severance Hall, December 15, 1940”) and in the Bach Cantatas Website discography; no session ledger was seen.

[1] [6] [7]
Place
Severance Hall, Cleveland Documented

Named in the Sony Classical box-set listing and in the Bach Cantatas Website discography; the Internet Archive description does not name the hall. That discography heads the entry “recorded live”; the issue is the commercial six-side Columbia set, and each file begins and ends in silence, with no applause.

[6] [7]
Label
Columbia Masterworks, set M-465 (written MM 465 in the Internet Archive description) Documented

The item description reads “Columbia 78rpm Set MM 465”; the 1941 review and the 1942 catalogue give “set M-465”. The review gives three discs at $3.50.

[1] [2] [3]
Catalogue
Columbia Masterworks set M-465; discs 11589-D to 11591-D Documented

The disc numbers are read from the OCR text of the 1942 catalogue, which lists the set as 6 sides with Krasner, the Cleveland Orchestra and Rodzinski; the page image was not checked.

[3] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
XCO 29764 to XCO 29769 (six sides); the take numbers are not given Documented

As given in the item description. Which sides carry the first movement is not stated.

[1]
Transfer
Digital transfer by F. Reeder Documented

Named in the item description, which adds “High bit rate”.

[1]
Transfer date
Not stated; the item was added to the Internet Archive on 17 September 2013 Unknown

The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

[1]
Processing
Digital transfer of the 78 rpm discs, described as high bit rate; equalisation and noise reduction are not described. Documented

The item carries one MP3 for each movement, uploaded as the original file.

[1]
Composition rights
Berg died in 1935, so the work has been in the public domain in the EU and other life-plus-70 countries since 2006; IMSLP also marks it public domain in Canada and in life-plus-50 countries. IMSLP considers it probably still protected in the United States. Documented

Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording.

[5]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; reviewed in September 1941 and listed in Columbia’s catalogue of 1942. Documented

The Internet Archive item carries a CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 licence label from the uploader. That label does not meet the site’s licence rules and is not relied on. The United States status of a 1940 recording is not established.

[2] [3]

Alban Berg, Violin Concerto, I. Louis Krasner, violin; The Cleveland Orchestra; Artur Rodzinski, conductor. Recorded 15 December 1940; Columbia Masterworks set M-465, reviewed in September 1941. Digital transfer by F. Reeder; Internet Archive item BERGViolinConcerto-NEWTRANSFER. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement

  2. The American Music Lover (later The American Record Guide), vol. 8 no. 1, September 1941 (Internet Archive scan) — Record reviews, pp. 17–⁠18: “BERG: Concerto for Violin and Orchestra … Columbia set M-465, three discs, price $3.50”. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  3. Columbia Record Catalog (1942) (Internet Archive, Media History Digital Library) — General list, Berg: Concerto, Krasner and the Cleveland Orchestra, Rodzinski, 6 sides, set M-465, 11589-D to 11591-D (OCR text). Accessed 2026-10-19.
  4. Michael Steinberg — programme note on Berg’s Violin Concerto, Boston Symphony Orchestra — Commission, Krasner’s visit to Berg in June 1935, description of the first movement and its folk song. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  5. IMSLP — Violin Concerto (Berg, Alban) — Public-domain notice (Canada, life-plus-50 and life-plus-70 countries; probably still protected in the United States); first publication 1936. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  6. Artur Rodziński, The Cleveland Orchestra — The Complete Columbia Album Collection (Sony Classical, 2023), listing on Discogs — CD 13: “Recorded: … Cleveland, Severance Hall, December 15, 1940” for the Berg concerto tracks. Accessed 2026-10-19.
